q1_issues.issue: The relative clause "in which one always cheats" becomes an unrestricted rule over every person, asserting that everyone cheats rather than that cheating happens in this game.
"always" is dropped — no frequency or universal-occurrence marker records it anywhere in the parse.

(Location (sk_cheat $x) game) uses the bare class symbol game for the specific game the relative pronoun "which" picks out (love itself), which the instruction set reserves for non-specific/generic objects, and treats an abstract game as a spatial container.

q2_gaps: frequency adverb "always" (and never/often/rarely) — the frequency section covers only named calendar slots, (Every e n unit) periods and (TimesPer e n unit) rates, so a universal-over-occasions adverb has no form
impersonal generic pronoun "one" ("one always cheats" = people in general) — the no-antecedent pronoun rule yields only an anonymous person witness, never a generic range

a full (non-reduced) restrictive relative clause modifying a predicate nominal with the relative pronoun inside a PP ("a game in which ...") — only participial reduced relatives and relative clauses inside rule premises are addressed, and nothing says how the clause attaches to the head kind or how "which" binds to it
notes: Statement 0 is right: the copular kind claim with an indefinite predicate nominal takes Inheritance at the empirical 0.9/0.9. The defect is confined to the relative clause, which is rendered as an unrestricted universal about persons.
